name: Khazanchi Jewellers Ltd
title: Khazanchi Jewellers Ltd - 543953 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Jewellery wholesaler-retailer reports FY26 EBITDA margin 6.19% and H2 margin 6.67%, but supply-side evidence is absent: no capacity or utilisation data, inventory days rising to 70-75 and a new showroom adding stock.

summary.headline: FY26 EBITDA rose 95.69% to INR126.99 crores at a 6.19% margin on total income of INR2,051.02 crores (+15.71%).
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of INR2,051.02 crores, up 15.71% YoY, with EBITDA of INR126.99 crores (+95.69%) and PAT of INR89.42 crores (+98.87%). H2 FY26 total income was INR1,098.26 crores (+8.1%), with EBITDA of INR73.21 crores (+102.79%) and PAT of INR50.72 crores (+103.6%). Management attributed margin gains to a shift toward higher-margin designer, diamond (Vajraa Diamonds) and retail products, and a new Chennai flagship showroom opened about two months before the call. Management reiterated 25-30% growth guidance and, in one answer, cited 35% PAT growth for FY27. The call was heavy on generalities, and several answers on inventory, KPIs and the gold-policy impact lacked hard data.

segments.name: B2B (wholesale)
segments.commentary: Serves over 1,000 clients per management, with more than 500 B2B clients served every year; management says 80-90% are repeat clients and no client exceeds 5% of volume. Ticket size not quantified.

segments.name: B2C (retail)
segments.commentary: Retail share of sales is about 10% today, with a target of 25% within about two years; retail margins cited at 10-12%. Chennai flagship has 10,000 sq ft total area and about 6,800 sq ft sales area, opened about two months before the call, with a INR450-500 crore revenue target.

segments.name: Vajraa Diamonds (diamond jewellery)
segments.commentary: Management says the premium diamond brand is gaining traction and has added to margins; no figures were disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Growth target of at least 25-30% a year, reiterated for FY27 and beyond.
In one answer, management said it is confident of achieving 35% PAT growth in FY27, citing higher margins from the new retail store.
Retail target of INR450-500 crores for the new store in the near future.
Retail share of sales to rise from about 10% to at least 25% within the next two financial years.
No fundraising planned; expansion to be funded internally.
capex_capacity: Chennai flagship showroom (10,000 sq ft total, about 6,800 sq ft sales area) opened about two months before the call.
Plans to open smaller-format stores initially in Tamil Nadu, later pan-India; location search under way, no count or capex disclosed.
Manufacturing is asset-light, using artisan units spread across India; no owned capacity or utilisation data given.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no slowdown in demand despite high gold prices; any dip lasts about 1-2 months.
Management described the government's request that citizens stop buying gold for a year as a short-term impact, expecting exchange and recycling of household gold to add business.
Management said no margin decline is expected from the gold-buying appeal and that gold price falls of 15-20% would have little impact on margins.

Working capital: management gave overall working capital cycle of 52 days and inventory cycle of 70-75 days, with the increase attributed to retail stocking. These figures were not reconciled in the call.
Management did not give a split of FY27 growth between gold price and volume.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins hold at current levels over the medium term if gold prices stay flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to designer and higher-margin items supports sustained margins and expects further improvement, without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle (inventory, receivable and payable days)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inventory cycle is 70-75 days and overall working capital cycle is 52 days, with receivables collected within about a week at most; the payable figure was not given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average ticket size in wholesale and retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Wholesale ticket size is not defined because it varies by client; retail average invoice size is INR1.5-1.7 lakhs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold-buying appeal affecting margins or top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no margin decline and any top-line effect would be short-lived.

qa_highlights.question: What is the projected sales for the new flagship?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a target of INR450-500 crores in the near future; it said sales per sq ft cannot yet be measured after two months.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 growth and PAT expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 25-30% growth and said it is confident of 35% PAT growth in FY27 due to higher retail margins.

risks_watch: Retail ramp-up: inventory days rose with stocking for the new store, and management gave a 70-75 day inventory cycle against a 52-day overall working capital cycle; the INR450-500 crore store target has not yet been tested.
Government gold-buying appeal and possible duty changes could dampen discretionary demand; management expects only a short-term effect.
Inventory of about INR400-408 crores is large relative to the scale of the business; watch whether inventory grows faster than sales.
Retail share target of 25% depends on store execution and is still to be delivered.
Guidance of 35% PAT growth for FY27 is above the stated 25-30% revenue target; watch for clarification.
Management gave little detail on KPIs, payables, cash flow, debt or capex, which limits the analysis.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and margins, with repeated reference to the 25-30% growth target. Answers on inventory, KPIs, working capital and the gold-policy impact were vague or hard to follow and lacked numbers.
key_quotes: So in near future also, the margins will surely improve.
In that, we have surely a higher margin bracket that is somewhere around 10% to 12%.
So we do not see any, what they say, reduction in demand or pain.
